visual_evidence.observed_frames: I inspected 1 fps frames from 205–212 seconds and the full frame at 210 seconds. The chest begins closed/outlined, then is visibly open by about 209–210 seconds; a bright small pickup-like glint remains near the lower-right of the chest area at 210–211 seconds. This supports a visible opened container and nearby item sparkle, but these low-resolution frames do not identify the exact dropped item mesh or its shader/texture. A source-backed montage is `.local-inputs/reference-video/dh2-act1/chest-sequence-205-213.jpg` and the direct frame is `.local-inputs/reference-video/dh2-act1/itemdrop-210.jpg`.
visual_evidence.version_limit: Footage is v1.0.3; the recovered native image/source receipts are v1.0.2. Any visual difference between those versions remains unknown.

logic_evidence.item_source: `port/level-world/reference/world-item-object-owner-v1/original-source.json` pins the original v1.0.2 image SHA and ItemObject constructor/init excerpts. ItemObject::InitOnce at 0x3ECE80 selects the authored `data/3D/GameObjects/itemdrops.bdae` resource, then copies the selected ItemAudioVisual row Visual string into its VisualObject node before GameObject::InitPost; if the visual object exists it calls VisualObject::ApplyMeshBox. ItemObject::InitAgain at 0x3EC0F0 takes AudioVisualID from the transferred ItemInstance and writes the selected row's source audio fields before physical-item setup.
logic_evidence.art_mapping: `source-itemdrop-scenes-v1.json` plus `itemdrop-source-assets-v1.json` establish ItemTable word21 -> AudioVisual row -> original itemdrops BDAE xref. Potion0 id925 uses row20 `dummy_itemdrop_Potion` (30 triangles, 44 vertices, 2 materials, static); GoldStack01 id418 uses row13 `root_itemdrop_Gold_01` (28 triangles, 50 vertices, one CharacterVisual controller). Both use `atlas_dh2_game_objects_001.tga`; Gold also references `atlas_dh2_game_objects_001_alpha.tga`.
logic_evidence.material_path: The interaction material binder now resolves each exact BRES source material against its selected pass. For external effects it loads the canonical source-cache resource data/gfx/effects/GL_Diffuse_L1_VC_iPhone.bdae, selects the authored #Multilight-fx effect URI and exact GLES2 CurrentTechnique material parameter, and requires one pass in that actual effect BRES. For local ProfileCOMMON it uses the original itemdrops.bdae effect row. The binder decodes source textures and applies the source root red-channel alpha merge rule where selected.

Resolve each original material to its source pass and source textures, retaining the exact pass data on each range. Preserve Potion static geometry and Gold authored controller rest pose; no drop motion policy is inferred.
uncertainties: Reference footage does not resolve which precise item visual is sparkling in the observed frames.
The existing visual proof is geometry/headless only; it does not establish original-game GPU shader output or runtime drop motion.

A second same-store fixture resolves Potion/Gold source passes, compares exact source texture pixels after alpha merge, asserts retained records/positions and 44/50 vertices, and sends a ready frame only to a capture callback (no GPU claim).

api.load: SourceWorldItemDropRenderV1::load(AssetCatalog&, RuntimeWorldItemAdapterV1&, ItemAudioVisualTable borrow, source material resolver, submit callback, output, error). Material resolver receives actual retained BRES material/range and a separate AssetCatalog containing the canonical external effect file at data/gfx/effects/.
api.frame: prepare() emits exact store identity/record/quantity/source position, source Visual URI, retained source mesh borrow and translation transform, plus per-draw source_pass_ready and frame renderer_ready flags. submit() rejects an unresolved source pass and otherwise hands the frame to the root-owned RenderQueue callback.
api.lifetime: Root must retain the submitted frame until every RenderQueue mesh/range borrow has drained. Root owns frame begin/end, camera, renderer state, and queue ordering.
